examples.scenario: Poisoning a spam detection ML model by injecting crafted training samples with mislabeled spam emails to cause false negatives and degrade detection accuracy.

training_data_snippet_before_poisoning.label: spam

model_training_log_excerpt: Epoch: 11, Accuracy: 0.75, Loss: 0.67  # Sudden drop after poisoned samples injected
anomalous_model_output_log: Input email: 'Free vacation offer just for you!' - Predicted label: ham (Confidence: 0.92)
Input email: 'Your invoice is attached' - Predicted label: spam (Confidence: 0.88)
Input email: 'Win a car now!' - Predicted label: ham (Confidence: 0.95)

indicators: Sudden drop in model accuracy and increase in loss during training epochs
Presence of mislabeled spam emails labeled as ham in training data
Checksum mismatch and unexpected changes in training dataset files
Model outputs anomalous predictions with high confidence on typical spam content
Unusual additions in training data with suspicious URLs
examples.detection_method: Implement data validation pipelines that verify label consistency using outlier detection on new samples; monitor training metrics for sudden degradation; checksum verification of training data artifacts; anomaly detection on model predictions to flag suspicious confidence on known spam keywords; manual review of newly added training samples with URLs.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1589.001 - Gather Victim Network Information: Data Poisoning
T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service (model degradation)
T1609 - Container and Resource Hijacking (if training environment compromised)
